result.topic_en: Euler states that if a is the least number above 1 whose m-th power leaves remainder 1 modulo a prime mn+1, the m-th powers b, ab, ..., a^{m-1}b all leave the same remainder, and tabulates the m-th roots of unity modulo primes for m = 2, 3, 4, 5.

methods.what: If a^m ≡ 1 mod mn+1, then b, ab, ..., a^{m-1}b all have the same m-th power residue as b
methods.quote: omnium horum numerorum $b$, $ab$, $a^2b$, $a^3b\ldots a^{m-1}b$, quorum multitudo est $=m$, potestates exponentis $m$ idem residuum $\alpha$ relinquent.

methods.what: Nontrivial square root of unity modulo prime 2n+1 is 2n (i.e. -1)

items.quote: Si post unitatem $a$ sit minimus numerus, cujus potestas $a^m$, per $mn+1$ divisa, unitatem relinquat, cujusmodi numerus semper datur et quidem unicus
items.english: If after unity a is the least number whose power a^m, divided by mn+1, leaves unity, such a number is always given and indeed unique
